title: Joint Interventional Equivalence of Latent Cyclic Linear Non-Gaussian Models
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field: the coupled law-set criterion is substantive, but separate-regime versus joint equivalence remains open and the requested restricted-class/explicit compiler guarantees are incomplete.
gap_reasons: The note proves a substantive sound-and-complete coupled law-set criterion through exact mixing realization, finite source partitions, simultaneous response matrices, and real-algebraic elimination, but it does not solve the advertised structural question of when separate regime equivalence implies joint equivalence.

The delivered population class also drops the brief's centering and finite-second-moment restrictions; equivalence for this larger moment-free class does not logically imply equivalence for the requested restricted law sets.

The explicit bit-operation bounds are not established by the cited quantifier-elimination theorem as written: the citation supplies asymptotic arithmetic complexity and intermediate bit-size bounds, whereas the manuscript asserts a particular closed-form bit bound and certificate output without deriving the conversion.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a finite coupled law-set criterion using exact mixing realizations, source partitions, simultaneous response matrices, and real-algebraic elimination, together with a strict intervention-refinement witness and a compact-subclass confidence construction. It did not determine when separate per-regime equivalence glues to one common mechanism, and the final note did not fully transfer the theorem back to the requested centered finite-moment class or instantiate the claimed compiler certificate and bit accounting. These gaps held the achieved tier to subfield, below the fixed field floor.
tldr: The paper gives sound-and-complete finite criteria, with certified compilers, for equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel law sets in latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models under both exact-support and zero-allowed graph conventions, for fixed observed and latent node sets. At the observational specialization, the zero-allowed theorem matches Dai et al.’s published model class; for a general finite intervention family it adds simultaneous principal-response constraints ensuring that one coefficient matrix and one source-law tuple realize every regime. The exact-support stratum engine combines affine and Hall–Rado realization, unrestricted visible-source partitions, and translation rigidity while retaining cancellations, invisible sources, and lower-dimensional strata. The paper also proves the moment-free square no-latent row and matching reduction, an all-parameter exact-support strict-refinement witness, and an honest compact-Laplace graph confidence superset.
gap: Existing results separately characterize observational law-set equivalence for latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, graphical intervention equivalence for latent directed acyclic graphs, or full parameter recovery under sufficiently rich second-order experiments. None gives an exact all-cancellations criterion for equality of full affine response-kernel model sets when the graph is exact structural support and one coefficient matrix and source-law tuple must serve every regime.
fill: The proposed criterion reduces admissible mechanisms to graph-generated affine and rank charts, reduces arbitrary source-law containment to finite proportional-column surjections, couples regimes through principal response matrices, and asks for an explicit certified compiler with a size-dependent bit bound. The inferential rung compares observable characteristic functions directly on a compact subclass.
